sentences.text: The name Melanorosaurus translates to "Black Mountain Lizard," combining Greek roots for black, mountain, and lizard.
Its skull measured approximately 250 millimeters in length.
The premaxilla, a bone at the front of the snout, held four teeth on each side, a feature typical of early sauropodomorphs.
The limb bones were notably heavy and massive, resembling those found in true sauropods.
The animal reached a length of about 8 meters and weighed roughly 1.3 metric tons.
A complete skull was not described until 2007, when it was cataloged under the number NM QR3314.
The original type specimens were discovered, described, and named in 1924 by Sidney H. Haughton.
Fossils were collected from the Lower Elliot Formation on the north slope of the Black Mountain in Transkei, South Africa.
In 2024, the specimen SAM-PK-3449 was designated as the lectotype following a redescription.
Under some definitions of Sauropoda, Melanorosaurus is classified as an early sauropod.
Adam Yates has proposed a definition of Sauropoda that specifically excludes Melanorosaurus, defining the group as sauropodomorphs closer to Saltasaurus than to Melanorosaurus.

The time range for Melanorosaurus spans from the Norian to the Sinemurian, approximately 227.3 to 192.9 million years ago, though its fossils were collected from the Lower Elliot Formation dating to the early Norian.
